posts.text:
A view function can cost gas, and a packed struct can cost more to update.

Five Solidity interview questions with short answers for the EVM and Solidity 0.8.x.
posts.alt: Solidity interview question SOL-F-04 asks the purpose of view and pure functions. The answer distinguishes an off-chain eth_call, with no network transaction fee, from the same computation inside a transaction, which uses gas. Scope: EVM and Solidity 0.8.x.

posts.text:
Q: How do storage, memory and calldata differ?

A: storage persists between calls. memory is writable scratch space for a call. calldata is read-only argument data. Use calldata for reference-type inputs you do not need to modify.
posts.alt: Interview question SOL-F-01 compares Solidity data locations. storage persists between calls; memory is writable temporary space for a call; calldata is read-only argument data. Use calldata for reference-type inputs that do not need modification.

posts.text:
Q: What is a modifier?

A: Reusable logic around a function body. Example: onlyOwner runs require(msg.sender == owner) before _;. The _; placeholder runs the body; code after it runs afterward.
posts.alt: Interview question SOL-F-02 with an example modifier: modifier onlyOwner() { require(msg.sender == owner); _; }. The caller check runs before the function body; _; runs the body, then any following code executes. This fragment assumes owner is defined and initialized.

posts.text:
Q: What are view and pure for?

A: view may read state but cannot modify it. pure may neither read nor modify state. An off-chain eth_call pays no network fee; execution inside a transaction still consumes gas.
posts.alt: Interview question SOL-F-04 compares view and pure functions. view may read state but cannot modify it; pure may neither read nor modify state. Both execute instructions. Off-chain eth_call has no network transaction fee; execution inside a transaction consumes gas.

posts.text:
Q: How does delegatecall enable upgrades?

A: Implementation code uses the proxy's storage and address, preserving msg.sender and msg.value. Upgrades change the implementation pointer; storage layout must stay compatible.
posts.alt: Interview question SOL-I-02 on upgradeable proxies and delegatecall. Implementation code uses the proxy's storage and address while preserving msg.sender and msg.value. Upgrades change the implementation pointer; the storage layout must remain compatible.

posts.text:
Q: How should you order struct fields for storage packing?

A: Group fields that fit in 32 bytes. uint128, uint128, uint256 uses 2 slots; uint128, uint256, uint128 uses 3. Fewer slots do not guarantee cheaper writes.

Fewer slots do not guarantee cheaper writes; gas depends on access patterns. Do not reorder existing fields in a deployed proxy's storage layout.
